title: TICKET-BENCH
bridge: TICKET-BENCH is like a Playwright suite for Nova itself: fixed cases, and a red check when a PR makes things worse. Except: each case is a whole past ticket, and the agent is not deterministic, so each task runs 3 times. Time and cost are measured, never limits.
intro: How do we know a change to Nova's harness, a skill line or a model setting helps? We run it on 40 real past tickets whose fixes we already know. This lesson mines the tasks and defines them for Harbor. BE and FE engineers curate 40, and every harness change is scored and gated.

sections.h: A bench made of our own past tickets
p: TICKET-BENCH is a fixed set of 40 past fcp tickets. Each one has a known fix and the tests that fix added. We hand Nova the ticket text on the commit before the fix, and grade its work with those tests.
Real tickets with real tests are the closest thing to pilot work. Mining them from merged PRs costs much less than writing tasks by hand.

Lesson p10-6 introduced Harbor, our bench runner, and its task folder. A task is a folder with instruction.md, task.toml, tests/ and solution/. The tests decide pass or fail by writing a reward to a file.
The bench data never goes into ai-agents or rnd-kb. It lives in a restricted golden-set repo, so the brain never indexes the answers. Its name is still to decide with Sean and Ronen.

callout.text: Bench code is Python in ai-agents/evals/, next to Harbor. Bench data lives only in the restricted golden-set repo, never where an agent can read the answers.

sections.h: Mining, part 1: what counts as a candidate
p: mine.py lives in the evals uv project. Part 1 sets the rules as regular expressions. A candidate PR must change tests and must not touch the paths the pilot leaves out.

kind() labels each task by the kind of change, from the Jira issue type and the paths. The kinds match readiness (lesson g4-1), so scores can be split the same way. The blank line between the helper functions is dropped to fit.
sections.because: We mine merged PRs that added their own tests, because those tests are a ready-made grade for the same ticket.

sections.h: Mining, part 2: one line per candidate
p: Part 2 lists merged PRs in the date range and prints one JSON line per candidate. The base commit is the parent of the merge commit, because fcp squash-merges: one commit per PR on main.
multi_file marks the big cases: 8 or more files across 2 or more top folders. The bench keeps 5 of them on purpose, to test workflows and parallel attempts (lesson g4-5).
The ticket text (summary, description, comments up to the merge date) comes from Jira with a read-only token. Attachments are never downloaded.
sections.because: We print JSON lines, because each line is one candidate a person can read, filter and pass to convert.py.

code.text:
prs = gh("pr", "list", "--repo", "RhinoHealth/fcp", "--state", "merged", "--limit", "2000",
         "--search", "merged:2025-01-01..2026-09-30", "--json", "number,title,files,mergeCommit")
for pr in prs:
    files = [f["path"] for f in pr["files"]]
    key = JIRA_KEY.search(pr["title"])
    if not key or not any(TESTS.match(f) for f in files) or any(EXCLUDED.search(f) for f in files):
        continue
    merge = pr["mergeCommit"]["oid"]
    print(json.dumps({"pr": pr["number"], "jira": key.group(), "merge": merge, "base": f"{merge}^",  # squash merges
                      "kind": kind(jira_issue_type(key.group()), files),  # read-only Jira call (helper not shown)
                      "multi_file": len(files) >= 8 and len({f.split("/")[0] for f in files}) >= 2}))

p: convert.py turns each candidate into a task folder. instruction.md holds the ticket text. tests/test.sh plus tests/hidden/ hold the PR's tests at their real paths. solution/solve.sh applies the merged diff; only Harbor's oracle agent uses it.
task.toml carries the metadata. Its field names depend on the Harbor version pinned in evals/pyproject.toml, so check the docs before you copy. Three blank lines are dropped to fit.
sections.because: We keep the tests hidden until grading, so Nova solves the ticket as written instead of reading the answer's tests.

code.text:
# tasks/fe-bug-1234/task.toml: in the restricted golden-set repo (name to decide). Field names per the pinned Harbor version.
version = "1.0"

[metadata]
kind = "fe_bug"                 # fe_bug | be_bug | add_tests | small_feature | dependency_bump
multi_file = false              # true for the 5 big cases that test workflows
source_repo = "RhinoHealth/fcp"
source_pr = 1234                # example values; convert.py fills them
jira = "RH-1234"
base_sha = "<parent of the squash commit on main>"
hidden_tests = ["frontend/test/unit/<file>.test.tsx"]
smoke = false                   # true for the 15 tasks in the smoke set
curated_by = "<BE or FE engineer>"
[agent]
# A far-away eval backstop only, to free a stuck eval VM. Nova itself has no time limit:
# minutes per task are measured and reported, and a timeout is reported as "stuck", not as a slow pass.
timeout_sec = 21600.0
[verifier]
timeout_sec = 3600.0
[environment]
# the task image carries Node 24 and the nova-worker harness tarball next to fcp's toolchain;
# the Python adapter runs `nova-worker run` inside it
# full size (8 vCPU, 32 GB) with FCP Lab and browsers; see README for the environment decision
cpus = 8
memory_mb = 32768

sections.h: The adapter runs the real Nova
p: Harbor runs an agent through an adapter: a Python class that starts the agent inside the task container. Ours is ai-agents/evals/ticket_bench/nova_agent.py. It starts the TypeScript harness CLI, nova-worker run <task.json>, on the base commit with the instruction.

So the task image carries Node 24 and the harness tarball from release-harness.yml next to fcp's toolchain. The tarball is one bundled file: nothing to install. The bench tests the same Nova that runs real tickets, on the same image.
Bench mode removes the people. The plan is approved automatically, and a question gets "no answer, use your judgement". There is no Jira, Slack or PR; the result is the working tree.
Answers must not leak. The checkout is reset to base_sha and git mirror refs are dropped. In bench mode the broker refuses the source PR and anything merged after base.

callout.text: Where trials run is still open; write the choice in ai-agents/evals/ticket_bench/README.md. Preferred: a fresh full VM per trial on Nova's AMI. Else: Harbor's docker environment inside one wide VM.

sections.h: Grading: the PR's tests and the neighbours
p: test.sh runs after Nova finishes. It copies the hidden tests in, over any edits Nova made to them. Reward 1 needs the PR's own tests to pass and the existing tests next to the change to pass too. A fix that breaks its neighbours scores 0.
Curation (G4-10) proves every task. Harbor's nop agent does nothing and must score 0; the oracle agent applies the real fix and must score 1. A task that fails either is fixed or dropped.

BE and FE engineers pick 40: about 12 fe_bug, 9 be_bug, 6 add_tests, 5 small_feature, 3 dependency_bump, plus 5 multi_file. They keep the ticket text as people wrote it, remove links to the PR, and mark 15 tasks smoke = true.
sections.because: A task whose tests pass without the fix, or fail with it, only measures noise, so each task is proven both ways.

code.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tasks/<task>/tests/test.sh: grades one TICKET-BENCH task. Harbor copies tests/ in only after the agent has finished.
# Reward 1 only if the PR's own tests pass AND the existing tests next to the change still pass.
set -uo pipefail
cd /work/fcp
BASE_SHA="$(cat /tests/base_sha)"                 # written by convert.py

cp -R /tests/hidden/. .                           # the PR's tests at their real paths; overwrites any edits to them
status=0

fe_tests=$(cd /tests/hidden && find frontend -name '*.test.*' 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^frontend/||')
if [ -n "$fe_tests" ]; then
  (cd frontend && npx vitest --run $fe_tests) || status=1
  (cd frontend && npx vitest --run --changed "$BASE_SHA") || status=1      # tests related to the changed files
fi

be_modules=$(cd /tests/hidden && find cloud -name 'test_*.py' 2>/dev/null | sed -e 's|^cloud/||' -e 's|\.py$||' -e 's|/|.|g')
if [ -n "$be_modules" ]; then
  ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud $be_modules || status=1
  ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud $(cat /tests/neighbour_modules) || status=1   # e.g. rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.services
fi
# client/ tasks: the same with `local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh client`

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; else echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; fi

notes.text: No -e: we want every test command to run and collect the status, not stop at the first failure.

The hidden frontend test files, as paths relative to frontend/.
Run the PR's own vitest files.
Then the existing tests related to files changed since base: the neighbours.
Hidden cloud test files turned into dotted module labels for Django's runner.
Run the PR's own backend tests with fcp's script.
Then the neighbouring modules convert.py listed.
Harbor reads the reward from this file: 1 only if every command passed.

p: pass@1 is the mean success rate over trials. pass^3 is the chance that 3 tries of a task all pass. It measures consistency: a task that passes once in three has pass^3 of zero.
pass_hat_k uses combinations. comb(n, k) counts the ways to pick k items from n. With 2 wins in 3 tries, comb(2, 3) is 0, so pass^3 is 0.
sections.because: A people-facing agent must pass reliably, not once in a while, so we measure consistency next to the average.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/ticket_bench/score.py: pass@1, pass^3, cost and minutes, split by kind. Python, next to Harbor.
import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from math import comb
from statistics import mean, median


def pass_hat_k(successes: int, tries: int, k: int) -> float:
    """Chance that k tries picked from this task's runs all pass (tau-bench's pass^k)."""
    return comb(successes, k) / comb(tries, k) if tries >= k else float("nan")

notes.text: The file's job: pass@1, pass^3, cost and minutes, split by kind.
comb(n, k): the number of ways to choose k things from n.
mean for rates and cost, median for minutes, so one slow run does not skew it.
The chance that k tries drawn from this task's runs all pass.
The name pass^k comes from the tau-bench paper.
Ways to pick k winning tries, divided by ways to pick any k tries. nan when there are fewer than k tries.

sections.h: Scoring, part 2: by kind, and the gate
p: score() groups trials by task, then tasks by kind. Cost per task comes from the gateway's run tag bench:<task>:<try>; minutes from Harbor's trial timings. Both are measured to learn, never used as limits.

An evalRun workflow (ai-agents/orchestrator/src/workflows/eval-run.ts) runs the bench on its own eval queue with fixed slots. So bench runs never take Nova's VMs, and only the orchestrator starts runs.

Some ai-agents PRs touch harness/, prompts, skills or the image. On those, a required check asks the orchestrator for a smoke run, 1 try per task. No workflow_dispatch. A drop of one task (about 6.7 points) means run again; two or more fail the check.

The full 40 run monthly with 3 tries on a Temporal schedule, and the trend goes to #ai-agents-alerts and the weekly review. A new rule in Nova's prompt or skills ships only if it raises pass@1 on the full set.

quiz.q: A task's hidden tests pass on the base commit, before any fix. What do curators do?

options.text: Keep it: a simple-looking task is still a task
options.why: Harbor's nop agent would score 1 on it. It measures nothing about Nova.

options.text: Fix or drop it: nop must score 0 and oracle must score 1
options.why: Each task is proven both ways before it enters the 40.

options.text: Lower its weight in the score
options.why: There are no weights. A task that cannot fail is noise and goes.

quiz.q: A harness PR drops the smoke set's pass@1 by one task (about 6.7 points). What happens?

options.text: The check fails and the PR is blocked
options.why: 15 tasks are noisy. One task is within noise, so it runs again.

options.text: Nothing; only the monthly full run counts
options.why: The smoke run is a required check on harness PRs.

options.text: The smoke run is repeated; two or more tasks lost fail the check
options.why: The gate is: a change must not lower pass@1, read with the noise of 15 tasks.

quiz.q: How does the adapter run Nova inside a task?

options.text: It calls the Anthropic API directly with the ticket text
options.why: That would test a different agent. The bench must run the real harness.

options.text: It starts nova-worker run on the base commit, from the harness tarball in the task image
options.why: Same harness, same image as real tickets, so the scores say something about the pilot.

options.text: It opens a draft PR and waits for Byte
options.why: Bench mode has no Jira, Slack or PR. The result is the working tree.
